subject: Better estimates in fragmented study area

messages.author: daf6ebfc0d0e2ebd
messages.subject: Better estimates in fragmented study area
parts:
Hello,

I have completed a summer of bird surveying in a very fragmented=20
combination of forest and grassland. I didn't stratify for various reason=
s=20
and decided to wait and post-stratify or incorporate covariates if=20
possible. It turns out the key species I=92m working with were all sight=
ed=20
within the forest patches. I=92ve considered breaking up transects and t=
his=20
doesn=92t seem possible because the fragmentation is too great. For=20
example, I frequently recorded individuals while walking transects throug=
h=20
grassland while I observed them in forest patches. Almost all transects=20=

are in an irregular, fragmented combination of grassland and forest. I=20=

have cover estimates for grassland versus forest for the area searched fo=
r=20
each transect, and I recorded the points along each transect where there=20=

was a change from forest to grassland anticipating this might help for=20=

stratification or developing covariates after the survey was completed.=20=
=20
It seems covariates should work somehow but I'm new to this. I also have=20=

an estimate of forested and grassland area for the entire study area=20
extrapolated from my cover estimates at transects. I=92m looking for advi=
ce=20
on how to make the density estimates better in this situation. Please=20=
reply to James at anders...@netscape.net. Thank you.

Also I was thinking (perhaps not too clearly) that maybe because all the=20=

sightings are in the forest this simplifies things a bit and I can still=20=
get a reliable abundance estimate without considering different strata. =

I=20
just analyze grassland and forest together and I can report the abundance=
=20
estimate as being for the forested area only. It=92s just the density th=
at=20
would be misleading because the birds are actually concentrated within th=
e=20
forest not spread out over all strata. Is this correct or wrong?=20=20

Cheers.

--

messages.author: 6e15de0134e98c08
messages.subject: Re: Better estimates in fragmented study area
parts:
Hi James, List,

I believe given your setting the best is to proceed as you suggested at=20
the end of your query. The density estimate you obtain, say D, will be=20
valid for the total area A (this assumes that the design was random with=20
respect to the two different habitats). Hence, the estimated total=20
number of animals is N =3D DA (for the combined grassland + forest area).=
=20
If you want Df, the density in the forested areas alone (which cover an=20
area Af, which you already have calculated), it is simply obtained by=20
N/Af. This assumes that there are effectively no birds in grassland,=20
which from your description seems a fair assumption.

Hope this helps,

Tiago
